questions.title: Summing Probabilities over an Inclusive Interval

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ has probability distribution given by $P(X = -2) = 0.10$, $P(X = -1) = 0.20$, $P(X = 0) = 0.25$, $P(X = 2) = 0.30$, and $P(X = 4) = 0.15$. Find $P(-1 \le X \le 2)$.

questions.title: Half-Open Range with Excluded Lower Endpoint

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with probabilities $0.05$, $0.10$, $0.20$, $0.25$, $0.25$, and $0.15$ respectively. Find $P(1 < X \le 4)$.

questions.title: Upper Tail Probability via the Complement Rule

parts.text: A discrete random variable $X$ has distribution $P(X = x)$ given by $0.08, 0.22, 0.35, 0.25, 0.10$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4$. Use the complement rule to calculate $P(X \ge 2)$.

questions.title: Conditional Probability of a Single Value Given Positivity

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has distribution given by $P(X = -1) = 0.10$, $P(X = 0) = 0.20$, $P(X = 1) = 0.25$, $P(X = 2) = 0.30$, and $P(X = 4) = 0.15$. Find $P(X = 2 \mid X > 0)$.

questions.title: Conditional Probability of an Even Outcome Given Positive Value

parts.text: The random variable $X$ takes values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities $0.10$, $0.20$, $0.25$, $0.30$, and $0.15$ respectively. Given that $X \ge 1$, find the probability that $X$ is even.

questions.title: Fractional Probability Table Interval with Mixed Signs

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values $-3, -1, 0, 2, 5$ with probabilities $\frac{1}{10}, \frac{2}{10}, \frac{3}{10}, \frac{3}{10}, \frac{1}{10}$ respectively. Find $P(-1 \le X < 5)$.

A discrete random variable $X$ has distribution given by $P(X = -2) = 0.12$, $P(X = -1) = 0.18$, $P(X = 0) = 0.35$, $P(X = 1) = 0.20$, and $P(X = 2) = 0.15$. Find $P(X \le 0)$ and hence find $P(X > 0)$.
Find $P(-1 < X \le 2)$.

questions.title: Direct versus Complement Evaluation and Prime Values

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 with probabilities $0.05, 0.15, 0.25, 0.30, 0.15, 0.10$ respectively. Calculate $P(X \ge 4)$ using direct summation, and verify the result using the complement rule.
Find $P(2 \le X < 6)$, and find the probability that $X$ is a prime number.

questions.title: Tail Probability and Conditional Probability of an Even Outcome

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 with probabilities $0.12, 0.18, 0.30, 0.25, 0.15$ respectively. Find $P(X \ge 2)$.
Given that $X \ge 2$, find the conditional probability that $X$ is an even number.

questions.title: Sum of Cards from Two Packs and Conditional Tail Probability

parts.text: Pack $A$ contains 8 cards numbered $0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 3, 3$. Pack $B$ contains 4 cards numbered $0, 2, 2, 2$. One card is chosen at random from each pack. Let $X$ be the sum of the numbers on the two cards. Draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Find $P(X \ge 3)$, and find the conditional probability $P(X = 3 \mid X \ge 2)$.

questions.title: Nonlinear Events and Conditional Probability Given a Squared Inequality

parts.text: The discrete random variable $X$ takes values $-2, -1, 0, 1, 2$ with probabilities $0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.25, 0.10$ respectively. Find $P(X^2 \ge 1)$ and find $P(|X| < 2)$.
Given that $X^2 \ge 1$, find the conditional probability that $X > 0$.

questions.title: Biased Die with Repeated Independent Trials and Conditional Multiple

parts.text: A biased 6-sided die has faces numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The score $X$ on a single roll has probabilities $p, p, p, p, 0.20, 0.20$ for $x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ respectively. Show that $p = 0.15$.
The die is rolled 3 times independently. Find the probability that a score of 4 is obtained on at most one occasion.
In a single roll of the die, given that $X \ge 3$, find the conditional probability that $X$ is a multiple of 3.

questions.title: Difference of Two Fair Spinners with Interval and Non-Zero Even Conditioning

parts.text: Two fair 4-sided spinners, each numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, are spun simultaneously. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be the numbers shown on the first and second spinners respectively. The random variable $X$ is defined by $X = S_1 - S_2$. List all 16 equally likely outcomes for $(S_1, S_2)$ and draw up the probability distribution table for $X$.
Find $P(|X| \le 1)$ and find $P(X > 0)$.
Given that $X \ge 0$, find the conditional probability that $X$ is a non-zero even number.
